statusDetail: Complete atomic audit of 58 checks across five representative public paths. Authenticated editing/account and donation flows were not covered.

page.notes: Server-rendered encyclopedia with Vector desktop and user-agent-selected mobile skin. Scope covers landing, reading, search, help and missing-title recovery; excludes authenticated editing, account creation, preferences persistence, donation and non-English editions.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct artifact inspection and mapped guidance comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: The desktop and prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshots are pixel-identical at 136,328 bytes and remain white, even though the CSS contains a dark media query and the UI offers a manual appearance setting.
The media query matched, the stylesheet includes reduced-motion handling, and no active animations were present.
Lighthouse passed color contrast and controls/text remained legible in captured templates.

The user can enter through Main Page, reach articles/search results, and navigate to help without an account wall.

Lighthouse measured LCP 1.6s, CLS 0 and TBT about 0ms; trace measured LCP 1.167s and no long tasks.

Loaded article/search/help templates remained usable without runtime errors; native document navigation preserves robust baseline behavior.

checkOutcomes.method: baseline/post heap comparison after 10 menu cycles
checkOutcomes.evidence: After 10 appearance-menu open/close cycles, node count rose only 0.57% (168,312 to 169,276); growth was mostly strings consistent with lazy initialization, not demonstrated unbounded retention.
Baseline self size was 10.72 MB with 168,312 heap nodes, proportionate for a script-enhanced encyclopedia article.
Neither baseline nor post top-constructor summaries exposed a Detached* population; jQuery object count remained 16 after 10 menu cycles.

principleOutcomes.reason: This emerging agent-facing principle does not apply to the public content and search journeys audited.

paths.description: Main Page, representing the editorial landing template and entry navigation.
Web article/disambiguation page, representing the core reading template and menus.
Search results, representing the primary find-content flow and form UI.
Non-existent article, representing HTTP/content recovery and alternative actions.

findings.summary: The default experience does not follow the system dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: The desktop and prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshots are pixel-identical at 136,328 bytes and remain white, even though the CSS contains a dark media query and the UI offers a manual appearance setting.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the automatic/default theme resolve from prefers-color-scheme and declare color-scheme so browser chrome and controls follow it; retain the manual override.

findings.summary: Article and navigation changes are abrupt rather than using cross-document View Transitions.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition rules or names on the multi-page reading experience.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } and stable view-transition-name values for persistent reading chrome, with reduced-motion behavior.

findings.summary: Dropdown and tooltip surfaces do not use CSS anchor positioning.
findings.evidence: The article exposes several checkbox-driven dropdown controls, while full stylesheet inspection found no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance menus and tooltips with CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks so overlays remain attached near viewport edges.

findings.summary: Transient menus are implemented with checkbox inputs rather than popover semantics.
findings.evidence: DOM and axe evidence show role=button checkbox toggles for main, appearance, language and tools menus; the page contains zero popover elements, dialogs, or details.
findings.suggestedFix: Use button elements with the Popover API and declarative popovertarget actions, preserving light-dismiss, keyboard and fallback behavior.

findings.summary: The desktop experience forces a 1120 CSS-pixel layout at a 360px viewport, shrinking the whole page to unreadable scale.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport, layout reported clientWidth and scrollWidth 1120 with visual scale 0.3214; the mobile screenshot shows tiny text and controls. The viewport meta is width=1120 rather than device-width.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and fluid/intrinsic layout rules; do not depend on user-agent skin switching to make a narrow viewport usable.

findings.summary: Components do not adapt to available container width.
findings.evidence: Full stylesheet inspection found no @container rule, while the narrow-viewport evidence retained the entire 1120px desktop composition.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type on reusable content/sidebar shells and use size-aware @container rules so components adapt independent of user agent and viewport skin.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus on the primary search field is not visibly outlined.
findings.evidence: After programmatically focusing the article search input, computed outline was rgb(32,33,34) none 3px and the only box-shadow was transparent/inset.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible ring with sufficient offset and preserve 44px touch targets across skins.

findings.summary: The reading page ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 87 KiB unused JavaScript in a 241,047-byte bundle and about 42 KiB unused CSS, including one inline ruleset with 97.2% waste.
findings.suggestedFix: Split ResourceLoader modules by reading-task need, conditionally load editor/analytics/language modules, and reduce shared CSS to rules required by the active skin.

findings.summary: The article template includes an image without alternative text and invalid ARIA roles on checkbox menu toggles.
findings.evidence: axe-core found one critical image-alt violation and five aria-allowed-role violations on the Vector menu checkbox controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the meaningful image an accurate alt value (or empty alt if decorative), and replace checkbox role=button patterns with semantic buttons/popovers.

findings.summary: Representative public pages omit a meta description.
findings.evidence: The Main Page and Web article probes returned no meta description; Lighthouse scored the meta-description audit 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate concise, page-specific meta descriptions from the lead summary while keeping titles unique and descriptive.

findings.summary: A session-identifier cookie is set without Secure or HttpOnly.
findings.evidence: CDP cookie inspection found enwikimwuser-sessionId with secure=false, httpOnly=false and SameSite=None on an HTTPS page.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark session identifiers Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is essential; avoid exposing identifiers to script.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced security policy is broad and incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers show CSP script-src permits unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval across a very broad host list, with no frame-ancestors directive or X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Move toward nonce/hash-based CSP without unsafe-eval, add frame-ancestors, and set explicit Referrer-Policy and least-privilege Permissions-Policy headers.

findings.summary: The primary search field explicitly disables browser autocomplete.
findings.evidence: DOM probe found the Search Wikipedia input has autocomplete="off" rather than an appropriate search autocomplete behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not disable autocomplete on search unless a documented privacy risk requires it; preserve useful history/suggestion assistance.
